paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Moses starts with a God who is dwelling place "through all generations," who was God before the mountains were born and who is God "from everlasting to everlasting" (Psalm 90:1-2). Then he looks at us, and we're like new grass that springs up in the morning and withers by evening (Psalm 90:5-6). Next to God, a life is a quick one, and Moses says it plainly so we can see where we actually stand.

Moses doesn't stop at the sigh, though, and that's the part I want you to carry out of my bakery. He prays, "So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom" (Psalm 90:12). I used to count falling dust, so trust me, counting days for a reason is a BIG upgrade. Our days are short, so the wise move is to live them close to the God who has always been our home, and to ask Him to teach us how.

And look at what Moses asks for next. He wants God's "loving devotion" in the morning so we can sing for joy, and he wants God's work shown to our children (Psalm 90:14, 16). Then he asks twice for God to "establish the work of our hands" (Psalm 90:17). So go bake today, friend, and hand the results to the God who lasts. Short days in His hands still count.
